$comment: DEBT-SEC-5. Subresource integrity for the third-party libraries this
repository RECOMMENDS but does NOT serve. dist/lib-manifest.json is the
sibling of this file and makes a different promise: it covers assets
scripts/vendor-closure.mjs builds and this origin serves. These are
chosen by the host page, so the guarantee here is the hash of a named
immutable build, not custody of the bytes.
Hashes are recorded rather than computed at build time, deliberately.
A network fetch inside the build gate makes CI non-hermetic and flaky.
jsdelivr versioned URLs are immutable, so a mismatch is an incident and
not drift. Run `npm run sri:verify` to refetch and diff.
CodeMirror 6 is absent on purpose. See the codemirror6 key below.

marked.note: The only required entry. MarkdownRenderer cannot parse without it.

highlight.js-theme.note: Declares no @font-face, so the hash covers the whole stylesheet.

katex-css.closure: stylesheet hashed; the 60 @font-face files it pulls are not SRI-able
katex-css.note: Same residual dist/lib-manifest.json records for bootstrap-icons.

mermaid.note: Mermaid 12 is published. This stays at 11 until the upgrade is reviewed.

viz.note: The standalone build embeds its WASM, so it fetches nothing at runtime.

reason: CodeEditor documents CodeMirror 6 as fifteen bare ESM import
specifiers from esm.sh. An integrity attribute attaches to a
<script src> tag and cannot attach to an import specifier inside a
module, which scripts/vendor-closure.mjs states in its own header.
Every one of those fifteen therefore arrives unverified, and so does
The specifiers also float at major @6, so the version is chosen at
request time. Pinning them is a separate decision, because the
fifteen packages have to interoperate at the versions chosen.
A consumer who needs the guarantee has two honest options: bundle
CodeMirror into one self-contained file and hash that, or serve it
from an origin they control. Neither is something this repository
